title: private-deployments-weekly-2026-06-08
content:
Private Deployments - Engineering Weekly 
Week of 2026-06-08
Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-private-deployments)
Collaborators: Marco Reyes, Lin Zhao, Priya Nair, Jonah Kim
Status: Draft (working notes / standup log)

1) TL;DR
- Installer 2.1 internal preview completed; upstream PR merged (PR-214). Smoke runs on internal VPC lab passed (single-region).
- Two customer blockers actively tracked (Customer A: VPC peering + routing; Customer B: on-prem KMS integration regression).
- Canaries for latest on-prem agent rollout scheduled for 2026-06-11.
- Next milestone: public beta for the simplified VPC onboarding flow targeted 2026-06-22.

2) Highlights / Wins
- Installer PR-214 merged: adds idempotent network checks and improved logging on failure paths. Marco led the work; Lin wrote the unit tests and integration harness for the VPC lab.
- Internal lab: three consecutive end-to-end installs in our rg-vpc-us-west cluster with persistent storage enabled; average provisioning time ~14m (down from 18m).
- Documentation: onboarding checklist and runbook updated on Confluence (linked).

3) Customer Blockers (open, high priority)
- Customer A (Enterprise banking customer) — JIRA-PD-4281 (priority: P0):
  - Symptom: Customer reports intermittent cross-account routing failures when connecting their AWS Transit Gateway to our VPC endpoint; flows drop during large model downloads (>2GB) causing model pull failures.
  - Recent actions: Networking team validated TGW attachments and route tables; found missing propagated routes for the peered CIDR range. We provided a temporary workaround (manual route propagation + lower MTU on the TGW attachment).
  - Current owner: Marco Reyes. ETA for fix: 2026-06-09 (apply propagated routes + automation to detect missing propagation during onboarding).
  - Next steps: After fix, run extended model-pull test (6GB) and coordinate with Customer A on a scheduled maintenance window.

- Customer B (Healthcare provider) — JIRA-PD-4302 (priority: P1):
  - Symptom: On-prem installer failing at KMS handshake step with an HSM-backed KMS (Yubico HSM) after upgrade to runtime 1.13. Root cause appears to be TLS renegotiation behavior change in runtime TLS lib.
  - Recent actions: Reproduced in our on-prem integration lab. Priya isolated the regression to the TLS client implementation in the new runtime build.
  - Current owner: Priya Nair (working with Cloud Security and Runtime teams). Temporary workaround: fall back to runtime 1.12 for affected customers.
  - ETA for long-term fix: 2026-06-18 (patch to runtime to respect HSM TLS renegotiation flags).

4) Standup / Daily Log (selected days)
- Mon 2026-06-08:
  - Goal: stabilize installer logs and add better failure categorization to reduce debug time.
  - Marco: landed improved network diagnostic hook; added clearer error codes (NET-PEER-MISS).
  - Lin: added integration test to simulate TGW route flapping; test now runs in CI nightly.
  - Priya: triaging KMS regression; reproduced with YubiHSM2 simulator and captured debug trace.
  - Jonah: prepping canary rollout plan + metrics dashboard (latency, install success, time-to-ready).

- Tue 2026-06-09 (planned):
  - Apply automation to detect missing propagated routes (test in staging).
  - Run expanded model-pull test with Customer A after automation is in place.

5) Installer / Release Notes (Installer v2.1 - internal preview)
- New: idempotent network checks, better error classifications, retry backoff improvements for large model pulls, additional logging around KMS handshake, and reduced default installation timeout from 30m -> 25m (based on lab improvements).
- Known issues: TLS renegotiation regression affecting some HSM-backed KMS providers (see JIRA-PD-4302).
- Rollout plan: internal preview -> selected customer canaries (6 installs) -> public beta (opt-in) -> GA. Canary start: 2026-06-11. Public beta target: 2026-06-22.

6) Observability / Metrics
- Installer success rate (last 7 days internal lab): 95% (target 99% by beta). Failures primarily network-related and KMS handshake failures.
- Average install time: 14-18 minutes depending on storage encryption and model bundle size.
- Dashboard: Jonah deployed a Grafana panel for install-time distribution and per-step failure counts. Link in Confluence.

7) Risks & Mitigations
- Risk: Large model pulls can saturate customer egress or transit gateways causing timeouts.
  - Mitigation: Add preflight bandwidth test and a throttled downloader with resume support; educate customers to prefer S3 signed URLs with multipart download.
- Risk: On-prem HSM integration regressions cause enterprise customers to remain on older runtime (security & compliance risk).
  - Mitigation: Fast-track a runtime patch and provide teammates with a tested fallback image; enhance KMS validation in installer before upgrade.

8) Action Items (owners + due dates)
- Marco: automation to detect missing propagated routes + staging test (due 2026-06-09).
- Priya: patch plan for runtime TLS regression + E2E validation with YubiHSM (due 2026-06-18).
- Lin: extend CI integration tests for TGW flapping and add a post-install network verification step (due 2026-06-12).
- Jonah: finalize canary rollout playbook and dashboard alerts (due 2026-06-10).
- Aisha: sync with support on customer communication templates and schedule Customer A maintenance window (due 2026-06-09).

9) Meeting Notes (Design review - 2026-06-07)
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Lin, Priya, Jonah, Security (KMS SME)
- Decision: Keep reduced default timeout (25m) for beta; allow override via installer flag for enterprises.
- Decision: Implement preflight network probe prior to model pull; probe will check MTU, bandwidth (10s TCP probe), and route propagation.
- Action: Security to sign off on TLS patch approach before runtime change is promoted.

10) Next week focus (2026-06-15 planning)
- Close Customer A blocker and verify in prod mirror environment.
- Deliver runtime TLS patch candidate and validate with three HSM vendors.
- Run canary installs (6 customers) and collect metrics for one week before expanding.
- Complete public beta docs and runbook updates.

11) Notes to self / open questions
- Do we need to throttle model download concurrency by default? (pros: reduces customer network impact; cons: increases install time) - bring to ops sync.
- Consider adding a small pre-warm cache for frequently used model artifacts for Dedicated customers to reduce first-pull pain.

---
End of weekly update.

(If you want these as separate daily standup snippets or want me to expand the runbook language for the public beta, tell me which section to prioritize.)
